chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: The Caesar's Palace incident and Sinatra's hands
summary: Collins describes the morning of the alleged fight at Caesar's Palace and says the story that Sinatra hit someone was untrue since his tendonitis made it painful to hold anything.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: No, this is at Caesar's Palace. But it's a funny thing. This man -- Frank had tendonitis, in both hands, and at this particular time he just was recovering from an operation and he could hardly hold the microphone in his hand. And this particular morning that he got into this little set-to -- I was on my way to mass, about 4:30 in the morning, and I was going through the casino, and he had been in one of the little rooms in the lobby of Caesar's Palace. And Gary Morton was there, and Lucille Ball, and I hadn't seen Gary in quite a while and so he saw me and he screamed John and we embraced and all of this.
In the meantime Frank came by and said, John, I'm going over and try my luck. Said fine, so my wife and I went

to mass, which was about, you know, a few blocks away. And in an hour we were back, and I didn't pay any attention to what was happening in the lobby but I got on the elevator and Pat Henry, who's a comedian, was on there, and he said, well Frank is not going to appear tonight. I said, why. He said he got into something here about gambling debts or something. Nobody could get the straight of it.

So I went back downstairs, and they said that Frank had hit one of the bosses, which was untrue. Frank couldn't hit anybody. His hands, I mean, it was just painful for him to hold anything in his hands. He couldn't hit anybody. But this is one of the misconceptions, you know, about -- I shouldn't say misconceptions, but this is one of the bad rumors that they put out about this man, you know. And that was entirely untrue, because he was a marvelous to me and to everyone I saw who worked for him.
